steps.title: Put Louisiana's arrivals in order
steps.prompt: Put the peoples who shaped Creole cooking in the order they came into Louisiana's story, starting with those already on the land. One stage did not happen.
steps: The Choctaw and their neighbours live on the land, growing corn, beans and squash
France founds New Orleans on the Mississippi
The first slave ships from West Africa reach the colony
Louisiana passes to Spain, whose cooks favour peppers, tomatoes and rice
Refugees from Saint-Domingue arrive by way of Cuba, bringing their cooks
Sicilian immigrants fill the French Quarter's markets and groceries
steps.distractor: British governors take the city from Spain and rule it until 1803
steps.why: The Choctaw and their neighbours were on the land first. France founded New Orleans in 1718, and slave ships brought West Africans from 1719. Spain ruled from the 1760s until 1803; Britain never ruled the city. Saint-Domingue's refugees came in 1809 and 1810, the Sicilians from the 1880s.

steps.title: Tell the Brennan's story in order
steps.prompt: Put the Brennan's story in the order it happened, as you would tell it to a curious table. One stage did not happen.
steps: Owen Brennan runs the Old Absinthe House, a bar on Bourbon Street
Owen opens Owen Brennan's Vieux Carré across the street
At Owen's request, the kitchen creates Bananas Foster, named for his friend Richard Foster
Owen dies, and Ella holds the family's restaurant together
Ella and the family open the restaurant at 417 Royal Street
The family divides: Owen's widow and sons keep Royal Street, Ella's side takes Commander's Palace
Brennan's closes after a foreclosure and a family dispute
Ralph Brennan and Terry White restore the house and reopen it
steps.distractor: Owen Brennan welcomes the first guests to 417 Royal Street
steps.why: Owen ran the Old Absinthe House before opening across the street in July 1946. Bananas Foster followed in 1951. Owen died in 1955, before the move, so Ella and the family opened on Royal Street in 1956. The family divided in 1973 and 1974; the house closed in 2013 and reopened in 2014.

steps.title: Order the old houses by their founding
steps.prompt: Put these New Orleans restaurants in the order they were founded, oldest first. One stage did not happen.
steps: Antoine Alciatore, a young cook from Marseille, opens his restaurant
Emile Commander opens his restaurant on a Garden District corner
Jean Galatoire buys Victor's Restaurant on Bourbon Street and gives it his name
Arnaud Cazenave, the wine salesman called Count Arnaud, opens his restaurant
Dooky Chase's opens in Tremé as a sandwich shop selling po-boys and lottery tickets
Owen Brennan opens his Vieux Carré restaurant on Bourbon Street
steps.distractor: Ella Brennan opens Commander's Palace in the Garden District
steps.why: Antoine's, from 1840, comes first. Commander's Palace comes next whether you take 1880 or 1893, then Galatoire's in 1905, Arnaud's in 1918, Dooky Chase's in 1941 and Brennan's in 1946. Emile Commander opened Commander's Palace; the Brennan family bought it around 1970.

match.title: Roots and what each brought

pairs: Technique, the roux and sauces built on stock
Peppers, tomatoes and rice cooked with meat in one pan
Okra, rice growing and cooking, and deep frying
Cooks from Saint-Domingue, where French, African and island cooking had met
Filé, ground dried sassafras leaves, with corn, beans and squash
Sausage and mustard making, credited with shaping Louisiana andouille and Creole mustard
